item.title: Anaplan
item.description:
Anaplan lets large organizations plan in a connected way. Instead of separate spreadsheets for finance, sales, and operations, teams build models on a shared platform so a change in one area, such as a drop in demand, flows through to inventory, headcount, and budget. Its modeling engine handles large multidimensional data, and planners can create scenarios to see the effects of different decisions before committing.

AI features aim to lower the barrier to building and using models. An assistant can help create or modify model logic from natural language, forecast with machine learning, and summarize results for decision-makers. The platform integrates with ERP, CRM, and data warehouse systems to pull in actuals, and offers applications for common planning needs, such as sales territory planning and supply chain optimization.

item.title: BigQuery
item.description: BigQuery lets teams analyze huge amounts of data without managing servers. You load data from files, databases, streams, or other Google services, write SQL, and BigQuery spreads the work across many machines and returns results quickly, whether the table holds millions or trillions of rows. Because storage and compute are separated and managed, there is no cluster to size or tune, which is a big reason analytics teams like it.

item.title: Bland AI
item.description:
Bland provides voice agents that talk on real phone calls. Companies use them to answer inbound calls, call leads, confirm appointments, and run surveys, replacing or supplementing call center staff. The agents speak naturally, handle interruptions, and can work around the clock.

Developers control behavior through a system of Conversational Pathways, which define the steps and branches of a call, along with tools to call APIs, look up records, and update systems. The platform supports many languages and voices, call analytics, and handoff to human agents. It offers APIs for scaling to large volumes of calls.

item.title: Bloomberg Terminal
item.description: The Bloomberg Terminal is the main workstation for traders, portfolio managers, analysts, and bankers. It delivers real-time and historical prices across stocks, bonds, currencies, and commodities, together with news, research, company data, and analytics. A command-based interface lets users call up functions with short codes, which is why people who use it daily rarely touch menus. Its messaging system, Bloomberg Chat, is also where much of the market does its dealing.

item.title: Buildium
item.description:
Buildium is designed for landlords and property managers who run a few dozen to a few thousand units. A manager can list vacancies, screen applicants, sign leases online, collect rent through a resident portal, and track maintenance requests with vendors. Owners can receive statements and reports, and community associations have their own tools.

Accounting is built in, with trust accounting, bank reconciliation, and tax reports that property managers need. Mobile apps let staff handle requests in the field. Some AI features help with tasks such as drafting messages and summarizing information, and integrations connect with listing sites, screening services, and other software.

item.title: ClickCease
item.description:
ClickCease deals with click fraud in pay-per-click advertising. When advertisers pay for each click on Google or Facebook ads, bots, competitors, and repeated clicks can drain budgets. The tool watches traffic, flags suspicious patterns such as repeated clicks from the same device or location, and adds the offending sources to block lists automatically.

A dashboard shows blocked clicks, estimated savings, and details about where bad traffic came from. Reports can be used to request refunds from ad platforms in some cases. Extras include tracking of invalid traffic on other channels and tools for monitoring ad campaigns and landing pages.

item.title: Clio
item.description:
Clio is a practice management system for small and mid-sized law firms. It keeps matters, contacts, documents, calendars, and communications in one place, tracks billable time, produces invoices, and takes payments through trust accounting and online billing. Client intake tools capture new inquiries and conflict checks, and a client portal lets clients view documents and messages securely. For many firms, it replaces a patchwork of spreadsheets and separate apps.

The AI assistant, Clio Duo, helps with the paperwork. It can summarize a matter’s documents and emails, answer questions about a case, draft correspondence, and suggest time entries. Clio has also moved into legal research and drafting by acquiring a legal research company, adding tools to find authorities and prepare documents inside the same environment. These tools aim to reduce the time lawyers spend on administrative work and first drafts.

item.title: Cresta
item.description:
Cresta works with customer service and sales teams. During a live call or chat, it analyzes the conversation and gives an agent real-time guidance, such as the next best response, a reminder to cover a compliance point, or a prompt to offer a relevant product. New agents ramp faster, and experienced ones get support on tough conversations.

After calls, Cresta scores interactions automatically against quality criteria, replacing the small samples that supervisors normally review. Managers see which behaviors drive better outcomes and can coach agents using real examples. Analytics surface trends in why customers call and where processes break down.

item.title: Decagon
item.description:
Decagon builds AI agents for customer service. Companies connect it to their help center, policies, and internal systems, and the agent answers questions, looks up orders, processes refunds, and handles account changes. It aims to resolve the issue instead of only deflecting people to articles.

A key idea is that support teams control the agent without engineers. They write instructions in natural language, called Agent Operating Procedures, that define how to handle scenarios, which keeps the behavior consistent and reviewable. Testing and monitoring tools show how the agent performs, and analytics highlight why customers contact support.

item.title: Deepnote
item.description:
Deepnote reimagines the Jupyter notebook for teams. Several people can edit a notebook at once, comment on cells, and run code on managed cloud machines without setup. It connects to data sources such as Snowflake, BigQuery, and Postgres, and supports SQL blocks alongside Python, so analysts can mix queries and analysis.

Results are easy to share. Notebooks can be published as interactive apps or dashboards with inputs, charts can be built without code, and scheduled runs keep outputs fresh. Version history and permissions help with team workflows, and it works with common libraries and Jupyter files.

item.title: Deputy
item.description:
Deputy is workforce management software for businesses with shift workers. Managers create schedules in a drag and drop calendar, publish them to staff, and employees see shifts in a mobile app where they can swap, pick up open shifts, or declare availability. Time clocks record when people arrive, and the data feeds payroll.

Compliance and cost control are big parts of the pitch. Deputy flags overtime and break rule violations based on local labor laws, forecasts labor needs against sales, and helps keep spending on target. Communication tools allow announcements and tasks, and integrations connect to payroll and point of sale systems.

item.title: DISCO
item.description:
DISCO helps legal teams handle the huge volumes of documents produced in lawsuits and investigations. Teams upload email, files, and chats, search and tag them, and decide what is relevant and privileged. The platform runs in the cloud, so reviewers can work together without managing servers.

AI features reduce manual review. Models rank documents by likely relevance, so reviewers see the important ones first, and generative tools summarize documents, answer questions about a set, and help build timelines. Law firms and corporate legal departments use it to cut review costs and speed up cases.

item.title: Dropbox Sign
item.description:
Dropbox Sign lets people sign documents without printing them. You upload a file, mark where each signer needs to sign or fill in fields, and send it by email. Signers open it on any device, sign, and the finished copy is stored with an audit trail that shows who signed and when. Templates make repeat documents such as contracts and NDAs quick to send.

The product started as HelloSign and was acquired by Dropbox, which renamed it. It connects with Dropbox storage, Google Drive, Gmail, Microsoft tools, and CRM systems, so documents can be sent from where they already live. A developer API lets software companies embed signing flows inside their own products, and Dropbox has added AI features in its wider document tools.

item.title: FactSet
item.description:
FactSet is one of the main data providers for banks, asset managers, and hedge funds. It aggregates information from many sources into a single platform: company financials, earnings estimates, ownership, supply chain relationships, news, transcripts, and market prices. Analysts use it to screen companies, build models, check ownership, and prepare reports, and portfolio managers use its analytics to measure risk and performance.

Delivery options range from the FactSet Workstation, an interface with analytics and charting, to data feeds and APIs that supply data to a firm’s own systems, and add-ins for Excel. Generative AI features let users search and summarize documents such as earnings calls and filings in natural language, and the company offers tools to connect its data to AI applications and agents. It also provides content for wealth managers and corporate users.

item.title: Filevine
item.description:
Filevine began in personal injury practice and has expanded to many types of law. It gives a firm a single place to track each matter: documents, notes, deadlines, tasks, communications, and billing. Workflows can be customized so that each case type follows the steps a firm wants, with automations that assign tasks and send reminders.

AI features help with the paper-heavy parts of legal work. They can summarize medical records and long case files, draft demand letters and other documents from case data, and help respond to clients. A document review tool extracts key facts and organizes them, which saves paralegals hours on cases with large volumes of material. Client-facing portals and text messaging keep people informed.

item.title: Freightos
item.description:
Freightos brings quoting and booking for international freight online. Shippers and forwarders enter details about a shipment and receive rates from carriers and forwarders, then book and manage the shipment on the platform. This replaces emailing multiple providers for quotes.

WebCargo is the air cargo side, used by forwarders to get rates and book space with airlines. Freightos also publishes the Freightos Baltic Index, a benchmark for container spot rates that is often cited in news about shipping costs. Its data helps businesses understand market conditions.

item.title: FullStory
item.description:
FullStory lets teams see how real people use their websites and apps. It captures sessions, which can be replayed like a video of the user’s screen, and detects signals such as rage clicks, dead clicks, and error clicks that suggest frustration. Searching across sessions helps teams find all users affected by a particular bug or those who abandoned a checkout step, instead of guessing from numbers alone.

Beyond replays, it offers analytics such as funnels, heatmaps, and journey maps, and tools for tying issues to revenue impact. AI features summarize sessions and surface patterns, so teams don’t have to watch hundreds of recordings, and help prioritize the problems that matter most. Privacy controls mask sensitive information, and integrations send findings to engineering and support tools like Jira and Slack.

item.title: Heap
item.description:
Heap approaches analytics with automatic capture. Once its snippet is on a site or app, it records user interactions without developers adding tracking code for each event. Product managers can then define what counts as a signup or a purchase later and look back at historical data, which avoids the gaps that come from forgetting to instrument something.

Analysis tools include funnels, retention, user paths, and session replay, and a feature that surfaces friction points and drop-offs. It supports building segments of users and comparing their behavior, and it can send data to a warehouse. Heap was acquired by Contentsquare, which combines its quantitative analytics with Contentsquare’s digital experience tools.

item.title: Help Scout
item.description:
Help Scout is for teams that want customer support without a heavy ticketing feel. Messages arrive in shared inboxes, where agents can assign conversations, leave private notes, and collaborate, while customers get replies that look like ordinary emails. That personal feel is a selling point for businesses that value relationships.

The product includes a knowledge base called Docs, a chat and messaging widget called Beacon, and reports on response times and satisfaction. Workflows automate routing and tagging. AI features draft replies from past conversations and help articles, summarize long threads, and adjust tone, and an AI answers questions for customers using the knowledge base.

item.title: HomeGauge
item.description:
HomeGauge is software for the home inspection trade. Inspectors collect findings on-site, add photos, and generate reports with standard language, ratings, and summaries for buyers and agents. Repair estimate features give clients an idea of costs.

The product has been around for years and has a loyal user base, along with scheduling and business tools. Newer rivals emphasize modern interfaces and automation, and AI features that draft report language.

HomeGauge is sold by subscription or license. Inspectors remain responsible for accuracy and compliance with standards of practice. Alternatives include Spectora, ISN, Horizon, Palmetto, and ITB. HomeGauge suits home inspectors.

item.title: HoneyBook
item.description:
HoneyBook is designed for people who sell services, such as photographers, designers, coaches, and consultants. A client inquiry arrives through a form, the owner sends a proposal with a contract and an invoice, and the client signs and pays online, all within a single flow. This replaces a patchwork of documents, email threads, and payment apps.

Other features support day-to-day work. Automations send reminders and follow-ups, a scheduler lets clients book meetings, and a client portal keeps messages, files, and payments in one timeline. Templates for proposals and questionnaires make repeat work faster, and AI helps draft emails and project descriptions. Reports show income and pipeline.

item.title: Housecall Pro
item.description:
Housecall Pro helps small service companies run their operations. Office staff schedule jobs and dispatch technicians on a calendar and map, customers receive confirmations and arrival notifications, and technicians use a mobile app to see their jobs, send estimates, collect signatures, and take payments on site. Invoices and payments flow into accounting.

The platform includes marketing and sales tools. Review requests, email campaigns, and a customer database help a business grow repeat work, and a booking widget lets homeowners schedule online. Some AI features answer calls and messages, help with scheduling and follow-ups, and summarize job details so owners can stay on top of the business.

item.title: Justworks
item.description:
Justworks is aimed at small companies that don’t want to run HR in house. The platform handles payroll, tax filings, benefits enrollment, time off, onboarding, and compliance in a single system, with a mobile app for employees. Its HR support team helps with questions about employment rules.

The distinct feature is the co-employment model. Justworks operates as a professional employer organization, which means it becomes a co-employer for tax and insurance purposes, pooling its customers to buy group health insurance and workers compensation at rates a small firm could not get alone. The business keeps day-to-day control over its staff and hiring.

item.title: Kaggle
item.description:
Kaggle is where many data scientists learn and prove their skills. Companies and researchers post competitions with real problems, such as predicting outcomes from data or classifying images, and participants submit models to a leaderboard. Winning solutions are often published, and the discussion forums are a rich source of techniques. Rankings and medals help build a public track record.

The platform offers more than contests. Public datasets cover topics from health to sports, free notebooks run Python and R in the browser with access to GPUs and TPUs within limits, and a models hub shares pretrained models. Kaggle Learn provides short, practical courses on Python, pandas, machine learning, and more. Benchmarks and community challenges around large language models have been added, and the site integrates with Google Cloud.

item.title: Keap
item.description:
Keap targets small service businesses and solo operators. It keeps contacts and conversations in one place, tracks deals through a pipeline, and uses an automation builder to send follow-ups based on what people do, such as filling in a form, opening an email, or paying an invoice. The goal is to keep leads moving without manual chasing.

It also handles the money side. Businesses can send quotes and invoices, take payments, set up recurring billing, and book appointments, which makes it common among coaches, consultants, and home service companies. AI helps draft emails and texts, and templates provide ready-made campaigns.

item.title: Klue
item.description:
Klue is a competitive enablement platform. Product marketing teams gather information on rivals from news, websites, reviews, and internal sales feedback, and organize it into battlecards with talking points, strengths, weaknesses, and objection handling. Sales reps access these cards in their CRM or Slack during deals.

AI helps keep the content fresh. It scans for changes, summarizes updates, and helps draft battlecard sections. Win/loss analysis tools collect feedback from deals and reveal patterns. Reports show which competitive content is used and how it relates to outcomes.

item.title: Kore.ai
item.description:
Kore.ai helps large organizations deploy virtual assistants. Companies design conversations and workflows in a low-code environment, connect them to back-end systems, and publish them on websites, mobile apps, messaging platforms, and voice lines. The assistants can answer questions and complete tasks such as resetting a password or checking a balance.

The platform has moved from rule-based dialogue to generative AI and agents. It supports large language models from several providers, retrieval over company content, and tools for building multi-agent systems, with governance features for testing and monitoring. Prebuilt solutions for banking, healthcare, retail, and HR speed up projects, and agent assist tools support human staff on live calls.

item.title: LegalOn
item.description:
LegalOn helps legal teams review contracts faster. A lawyer opens a draft in Word, and the tool checks it against a review checklist, highlighting risky or missing clauses and suggesting alternative wording. The checklists are built by lawyers, which the company says makes the guidance reliable.

Beyond review, the platform offers features for contract creation and management, and AI that answers questions about legal matters and compares language across documents. It started in Japan under the name LegalForce, where it grew quickly, and has expanded into North America and Europe.

item.title: LegalZoom
item.description:
LegalZoom helps people handle common legal tasks without a law firm. Users answer questions online, and the service prepares and files documents for things like forming an LLC or corporation, creating wills and trusts, registering trademarks and copyrights, and handling name changes. Registered agent services, compliance filings, and business licenses are available for new companies.

Human help is available at higher levels. Plans can include attorney consultations, document review, and legal advice subscriptions, and some tasks are reviewed by staff before filing. The company has added AI tools to guide users through forms, answer questions, and speed up document preparation, though legal advice itself comes from licensed professionals.

item.title: Legora
item.description:
Legora is a legal AI company from Sweden that has expanded globally. Lawyers use its assistant for tasks such as reviewing contracts and extracting key terms across many documents, researching legal questions, summarizing materials, and drafting and revising documents. A Word add-in brings these abilities into the editor where lawyers already work, so suggestions appear as tracked changes.

The platform emphasizes collaboration and structure. Features such as tabular review let teams compare many documents side by side in a grid, workflows capture a firm’s preferred processes, and shared workspaces allow lawyers and clients to work together. Firms can customize the system with their own playbooks and precedents, and security features aim to meet the confidentiality needs of legal practice.

item.title: lemlist
item.description:
lemlist helps sales teams and agencies reach prospects at scale. Users build sequences that combine email, LinkedIn steps, and phone tasks, and personalize messages with variables such as name and company. The brand made its name with personalized images and videos that change for each recipient, a way to stand out in crowded inboxes.

Deliverability is a major part of the product. Inbox warm-up gradually builds sender reputation, and tools check domains and monitor placement so emails land in primary inboxes, not spam. A lead database lets users find contacts and verify emails, and AI helps write openers and suggest follow-ups.

item.title: LexisNexis Protégé
item.description:
Protégé is the AI layer of LexisNexis’s legal research platform. Lawyers can ask research questions in plain language and receive answers that cite cases, statutes, and secondary sources from the LexisNexis collection, with links to the underlying authorities. It can summarize documents, compare them, extract key terms, and draft memos and clauses, and it connects with the Shepard’s citation service to help check whether authorities are still good law.

Newer versions emphasize agentic work and the lawyer’s workflow. Protégé can break a task into steps, such as gathering documents, researching issues, and producing a draft, and works in Microsoft Word so suggestions appear in the document being edited. Firms can customize it with their own documents and playbooks, and security terms are designed for confidential client information.

item.title: LivePerson
item.description:
LivePerson began with live chat and developed into a conversational platform. Brands use it to let customers message them on the channels they already use, with a mix of human agents and automated assistants. The platform manages the conversations, routes them to the right team, and records the data.

AI is central. Bots handle common requests, such as order status or billing questions, and hand off to agents when needed, and agent assist tools suggest responses. The company offers tools for building and managing assistants powered by large language models, with guardrails and analytics to check quality and compliance. Customers include banks, telecoms, and retailers.

item.title: Matillion
item.description:
Matillion is a data integration platform. Data teams use a visual designer to extract data from sources, load it into a cloud warehouse, and transform it there using the warehouse’s own compute. This ELT approach scales with the warehouse and keeps data in the company’s environment.

AI has become part of the product through Maia, a set of agents that act as virtual data engineers. A user describes what they need, and Maia can create pipelines, suggest fixes when something fails, and write documentation. Humans stay in the loop and can review the generated work. The platform also supports orchestration, scheduling, and version control with Git.

item.title: Meltano
item.description:
Meltano treats data integration like software development. A project defines extractors and loaders in a configuration file, and Meltano runs them to move data from sources into a warehouse. Because everything is code, pipelines live in Git, run in CI, and can be reviewed like other changes.

It builds on the Singer standard, which has hundreds of community connectors, and integrates with dbt for transformations and Airflow for orchestration. Teams can write custom connectors with a software development kit, which is handy for sources that commercial tools do not cover.

item.title: Microsoft Clarity
item.description:
Clarity shows how people really use a website. A snippet of code installed on the site captures sessions, which can be replayed like a video, along with heatmaps that show where visitors click and how far they scroll. It automatically flags signs of frustration, including rage clicks, dead clicks, excessive scrolling, and JavaScript errors, so teams can focus on pages where users struggle.

AI features add convenience. Copilot summarizes many sessions to surface common issues and gives answers to questions about user behavior, and filters let you segment by device, country, and traffic source. Clarity also offers insights on how AI chatbots and search drive traffic to a site. It integrates with Google Analytics, Microsoft Advertising, and platforms such as Shopify and WordPress.

item.title: Microsoft Dynamics 365
item.description:
Dynamics 365 combines CRM and ERP in a modular set of cloud applications. The sales and customer service apps manage leads, opportunities, cases, and customer communications, while finance, supply chain, and Business Central handle accounting, inventory, purchasing, and operations. Because the modules share a data platform, a company can start with one and add others over time, and they connect closely with Microsoft 365, Teams, and Power BI.

Copilot is built throughout. In sales, it summarizes accounts and meetings, drafts emails, and suggests next steps. In service, it helps agents find answers and summarize cases, and in finance and supply chain, it supports tasks like reconciliations, collections, and spotting disruptions. AI agents take on routine tasks, such as qualifying leads or processing orders, and Copilot Studio lets companies build their own.

item.title: Mindtickle
item.description:
Mindtickle is a sales readiness platform. New hires follow structured learning paths with lessons and quizzes, and practice pitches by recording videos or role-playing with AI, receiving feedback. Managers review the practice and see how reps compare on skills.

The platform links training to results. It tracks which skills correlate with success, identifies gaps across a team, and connects with CRM data to see how readiness affects performance. AI features generate content, score practice sessions, and recommend coaching.

item.title: Mixpanel
item.description:
Mixpanel helps product teams understand behavior. You send events from your product, such as sign-ups, searches, and purchases, along with properties about users, and Mixpanel turns them into reports. Funnels show where people drop off, retention charts show who comes back, flows map the paths people take, and cohorts group users by behavior. Self-serve reports let product managers and marketers answer questions without writing SQL.

The platform includes more than charts. Session replay shows what users actually did, feature flags and experiments test changes, and lexicon tools manage the data schema. AI features let people ask questions in plain language and generate reports, summarize findings, and surface anomalies. Data can be connected from warehouses, and Mixpanel integrates with tools for marketing, support, and customer data pipelines.

item.title: MoEngage
item.description:
MoEngage is built for brands with mobile apps and large user bases. It collects behavior data such as app opens, purchases, and browsing, then lets marketers segment users and design campaigns across channels. Journeys can be built visually, so a user who abandons a cart gets a push notification, then an email if they don’t respond.

Analytics show how campaigns perform and how users move through funnels. AI features predict who is likely to churn or buy, choose the best time to send each message, and suggest content, and a generative assistant helps write copy. The platform integrates with data warehouses and other tools, and operates worldwide, with a strong presence in Asia.

item.title: o9 Solutions
item.description:
o9 targets the planning process in big supply chains. Instead of separate systems for forecasting, inventory, production, and finance, it builds one connected model of the business, called the Enterprise Knowledge Graph, so a change in demand updates the supply plan and the financial outlook. Planners can run what-if scenarios to compare options before choosing.

Machine learning forecasts demand using sales history, promotions, weather, and other signals, and the platform recommends actions such as shifting inventory or changing production. Generative AI features let planners ask questions in natural language and summarize risks. Customers include consumer goods, retail, and manufacturing companies with complex networks.

item.title: Optimizely
item.description:
Optimizely began as an A/B testing tool and grew into a suite for digital experiences. Teams use web experimentation to compare versions of pages, feature experimentation to test changes in apps behind feature flags, and personalization to show different content to different audiences. Statistical engines determine which variations win, and rollouts can be controlled to reduce risk.

The platform also includes content management and commerce. A CMS lets marketers create and manage web content, and commerce products support B2B and B2C stores, so a company can build, publish, test, and optimize in a single environment. AI features, under the Opal brand, help generate content, suggest experiment ideas, and run agents that automate steps in marketing workflows.

item.title: Oracle NetSuite
item.description:
NetSuite was one of the first cloud ERP systems and is widely used by growing companies. A single system runs financials, inventory, procurement, order management, billing, and customer relationship management, so departments work from the same data instead of reconciling spreadsheets. Industry editions adapt it for areas like wholesale distribution, manufacturing, retail, and software, and it supports multiple subsidiaries, currencies, and tax rules, which suits companies expanding internationally.

AI features sit across the suite. Generative tools can summarize records, draft emails and descriptions, and answer questions about data in plain language, while machine learning supports forecasting, anomaly detection, and automation of accounting tasks like matching invoices. Reporting and analytics tools let finance teams build dashboards, and SuiteScript and workflows allow customization.

item.title: Paychex
item.description:
Paychex is one of the largest payroll providers in the United States. Businesses use it to pay employees, file payroll taxes, manage time and attendance, administer retirement and health benefits, and handle HR tasks such as onboarding and compliance. A defining feature is access to human specialists, which suits owners who do not want to figure out payroll rules on their own.

The Paychex Flex platform pulls these services into one system with mobile apps for employees and managers. AI features assist with answering HR questions, flagging payroll errors, and analyzing workforce data. The company also offers professional employer organization services, in which it co-employs workers and takes on benefits and compliance responsibilities. It acquired Paycor, a provider of HR and payroll software, to move further into mid-sized businesses.

item.title: Paycom
item.description:
Paycom is an HR and payroll platform built on one database for all functions. Employers manage hiring, onboarding, time and attendance, payroll, benefits, performance, and learning in a unified system, so data entered once appears everywhere. This design is meant to reduce errors from syncing separate tools.

Its best-known idea is Beti, which stands for Better Employee Transaction Interface. Employees review and approve their own timecards, expenses, and paid time off before payroll is run, which pushes corrections to the person who knows the data best and reduces payroll mistakes. Paycom has also added AI assistants for HR questions and tasks.

item.title: Paylocity
item.description:
Paylocity provides cloud HR and payroll software, primarily for mid-sized companies. Employers run payroll, manage benefits enrollment, track time and scheduling, handle onboarding and performance, and report on workforce data, all within one platform. A mobile app lets employees see pay stubs, request time off, and update details.

The company emphasizes employee experience and community features, such as company feeds, recognition, and surveys, in addition to core payroll. An AI assistant answers employee questions about pay, benefits, and company policy using the employer’s data, and helps managers and HR with drafting and analysis, which reduces the number of routine tickets.

item.title: Pendo
item.description:
Pendo helps product teams understand and improve their software. After adding a snippet to an application, Pendo records usage automatically: which pages and features people use, where they drop off, and how behavior varies by customer or segment. Product managers use dashboards, funnels, and retention reports to decide what to build and what to fix.

The platform lets teams act on insights without waiting for developers. In-app guides, tooltips, announcements, and checklists guide users through features, surveys and NPS collect feedback, and a roadmap tool captures feature requests. Session replay shows what people did, and AI features summarize feedback, suggest improvements, and analyze conversations with AI features inside products, which is a growing need as software adds assistants.

item.title: Pigment
item.description:
Pigment is a modern take on planning software. Finance teams build models of their company, including headcount, revenue, and spend, in an environment that feels familiar to spreadsheet users but works with large data volumes and multiple dimensions. Plans link across departments, so a hiring plan updates the budget automatically.

It supports scenario planning, which lets teams test the impact of different assumptions side by side, and produces dashboards and reports for executives. AI agents help analyze variances, generate commentary, and build parts of models from prompts. Integrations bring in data from ERP and CRM systems and data warehouses.

item.title: Planhat
item.description:
Planhat is a customer platform built for subscription businesses. It connects to a company’s tools and data, builds a profile for each account, and shows health, usage trends, revenue, and conversations in one place. Teams use it to prepare for renewals and spot upsell opportunities.

Automation and workflows trigger tasks and outreach when something changes, such as a drop in usage or an upcoming renewal. Dashboards and reports show retention and growth, and AI summarizes accounts and suggests actions.

item.title: Plausible
item.description:
Plausible keeps analytics simple. A tiny script collects page views, visitors, referrers, devices, and locations without using cookies or storing personal data, so most sites do not need a consent banner for it. The dashboard fits on a single page, which makes it quick to read for people who don’t want to learn a complex tool.

It supports goals and events, so site owners can track signups or purchases, and funnels for conversion steps. Features like UTM tracking and a stats API round out the basics. The code is open source, and users can self-host a free community edition or pay for the hosted service, which is run from European servers.

item.title: Postscript
item.description:
Postscript focuses on text message marketing for online stores. It connects to Shopify, collects subscribers through popups and checkout opt-ins, and lets merchants send campaigns about sales and product launches. Automated flows trigger messages for events like abandoned carts, browse behavior, and order updates, which tend to produce strong results.

Segmentation uses shopping data, such as purchase history and product interest, to tailor messages. Two-way conversations let customers reply and get help from a team member, and an AI assistant helps draft messages and suggests offers. Analytics tie texts to revenue so merchants can see what pays off.

item.title: Qlik
item.description: Qlik is known for its associative engine, which treats all the data in an app as connected. When you click a value in a chart, everything else updates to show related data, and values that are unrelated are shown as excluded, which helps users discover connections they did not think to query. This differs from tools that require predefined queries and has been a selling point for business users exploring data.

item.title: Remote
item.description:
Remote is a global employment platform. A company that wants to hire someone in another country normally needs a legal entity there, which is slow and costly. With Remote as the employer of record, the worker is legally employed by Remote locally, while the company directs their daily work. Remote handles contracts, payroll, taxes, benefits, and statutory requirements.

The platform also supports contractors, offers tools for onboarding, expenses, and equipment, and provides local compliance knowledge across many countries. A global payroll product helps companies that already have entities coordinate payments, and AI features assist HR teams with questions and workflows. The company has built its own entities in many countries rather than relying on partners.

item.title: Retell AI
item.description:
Retell provides the infrastructure for voice agents. A developer defines an agent’s prompt and tools, connects a phone number, and the platform handles speech recognition, the language model, speech synthesis, and call control with natural turn-taking and interruption handling.

Use cases include answering customer calls, scheduling appointments, qualifying leads, and following up with customers. Integrations with calendars and CRMs let agents take actions, and analytics show call outcomes. Handoff to humans is supported.

item.title: Rocket Lawyer
item.description:
Rocket Lawyer is aimed at people who need legal help without a full law firm engagement. Members answer questions in an interview format and the service generates documents such as lease agreements, NDAs, wills, and operating agreements. Documents can be signed electronically and stored, and templates are tailored to the user’s state.

Beyond documents, membership gives access to attorneys through ask-a-lawyer services and, for some matters, discounted consultations. Small businesses use it for formation, contracts, and compliance support. AI tools help explain legal terms and draft documents, and are positioned as a way to get started before consulting a professional.

item.title: SAP Concur
item.description:
Concur is a staple of corporate finance. Employees book travel, capture receipts with a phone, and submit expense reports, which flow through approvals and into accounting systems. Policies are applied automatically, flagging out-of-policy spending, and credit card feeds reduce manual entry. Finance teams use it to control costs, reimburse employees, and meet audit requirements.

The platform has grown to include invoice and travel management, with integrations to airlines, hotels, and payment providers. AI supports automatic receipt reading, categorization, audit of expenses to detect errors or fraud, and assistance through SAP’s Joule for answering questions and completing tasks. Reporting provides visibility into travel and spending trends.

item.title: Sierra
item.description:
Sierra focuses on replacing scripted chatbots with agents that can actually resolve customer issues. Companies such as consumer brands and subscription services deploy Sierra agents to answer questions, process returns, change plans, schedule appointments, and handle other tasks by connecting to back-end systems. The agent follows the company’s policies and tone, and hands off to a human when needed.

Several elements distinguish its approach. An Agent OS provides the tools for building, testing, and monitoring agents, with simulation and evaluation to catch problems before customers see them, and supports voice and messaging channels. The company often uses outcome-based pricing, where customers pay for resolved conversations instead of seats, which aligns cost with value. It combines multiple language models to improve reliability.

item.title: Smartlead
item.description:
Smartlead is built for outbound email at scale. Users connect many mailboxes, and the platform spreads sends across them, adjusts volume, and warms up new accounts so messages reach inboxes. Sequences, follow-ups, and reply management handle campaign logic.

Agencies value its multi-client workspaces, unified inbox, and analytics. AI helps personalize openers and classify replies. Integrations connect with lead databases and CRMs.

Smartlead is paid, with plans by active leads and emails. Cold email is regulated, and sending at scale damages domains if done badly. Alternatives include Instantly, lemlist, Apollo, Reply.io, and Woodpecker. Smartlead suits agencies and outbound teams.

item.title: Storylane
item.description:
Storylane is an interactive demo platform. A user records their product with a browser extension that captures screenshots or the underlying page, then adds hotspots, tooltips, and callouts to guide viewers through a story. The result is a demo that prospects can click through on their own, without needing a sandbox or a live call.

Teams use it across the sales cycle. Marketing embeds demos on landing pages, sales sends personalized versions in outreach emails, and customer success uses them for onboarding. AI features add voiceovers, translations into other languages, and personalization of names and logos for each prospect. Analytics show who viewed a demo and where they dropped off.

item.title: Streamlit
item.description: Streamlit is built for data scientists who want to share work without learning web development. You write a Python script and add calls like text input, sliders, charts, and buttons, and Streamlit produces an interactive web app that reruns the script when the user changes something. This model is simple enough that people can make an app in minutes, and it has become a standard for internal tools and demos.

item.title: SurveyMonkey
item.description:
SurveyMonkey is one of the best-known survey tools. Users create surveys with a drag-and-drop builder, choose from templates for customer satisfaction, employee engagement, market research, and events, and share them by link, email, or embedding. Question logic, branching, and randomization allow more sophisticated designs, and responses appear in real time with charts and filters.

AI features aim to make surveys better and analysis quicker. The assistant can build a survey from a description, suggest improved wording to avoid bias, and analyze open-ended responses by identifying themes and sentiment. A panel service lets researchers purchase responses from target audiences, and integrations connect results to tools like Salesforce, Slack, and Tableau.

item.title: Synthflow
item.description:
Synthflow is a no-code voice agent platform. A user designs the call flow in a visual editor, picks a voice, connects a phone number, and the agent handles calls, such as answering questions, booking appointments, and qualifying leads. Integrations connect calendars and CRMs.

Agencies resell the platform with white-label options, building agents for dental offices, home services, and similar businesses. Analytics show call outcomes and transcripts.

Synthflow is paid, with plans by minutes. Voice agents need testing for accuracy and disclosure of AI use. Alternatives include Retell AI, Vapi, Bland AI, Air AI, and PolyAI. Synthflow suits agencies and small businesses deploying voice agents.

item.title: Syte
item.description:
Syte brings visual search to e-commerce. A shopper uploads a photo or taps on an image, and the system finds similar items in the store’s catalog. Computer vision also tags products with detailed attributes, which improves search, filters, and recommendations.

Retailers use it for shop-the-look features, similar item suggestions, and personalization. Integrations work with common e-commerce platforms, and generative AI supports conversational shopping assistants.

Syte is sold to retailers on subscription. Alternatives include Algolia, Bloomreach, Vue.ai, Klevu, and Google Lens integrations. Syte suits fashion and home retailers with large catalogs.

item.title: Teachable
item.description:
Teachable is a platform for people who want to sell what they know. A creator uploads video lessons, text, and quizzes, organizes them into a course, sets a price, and publishes it on a branded school site. Students enroll, pay, and track their progress, and the creator gets sales and engagement data.

The platform handles the business side. It processes payments in many currencies, supports subscriptions, bundles, and coupons, and offers tools for affiliate programs and email marketing. Coaching products and downloadable files can be sold alongside courses, and certificates reward completion. AI features help draft course outlines and descriptions.

item.title: Thinkific
item.description:
Thinkific is an online course platform. Creators build courses from video, audio, text, and quizzes, organize them into chapters, and host them on a site with their own branding and domain. Students log in to learn, and the platform tracks completion and issues certificates.

Features extend beyond courses. Memberships and communities keep learners engaged, bundles and subscriptions provide pricing options, and integrations connect with email tools, payment processors, and Zapier. Businesses also use Thinkific to train customers, partners, and employees, and AI tools help generate course outlines and quiz questions.

item.title: UKG
item.description:
UKG is a major provider of human capital management software. Employers use it to run payroll, track time and attendance, schedule shifts for hourly workers, manage benefits, hire, and develop employees. It is especially strong in industries with large hourly workforces such as retail, healthcare, and manufacturing, where scheduling and labor compliance are complex.

AI is woven into the products. Its assistant helps managers and employees answer questions and complete tasks, analytics predict turnover and scheduling needs, and tools suggest schedules that balance demand, cost, and employee preferences. The company has multiple product lines, including UKG Pro for larger organizations and UKG Ready for mid-sized companies.

item.title: Virtual Staging AI
item.description:
Virtual Staging AI is built for property listings. An agent uploads a photo of an empty room, selects a room type and style, and the AI places furniture and decor that fits the space. Results arrive in minutes, so listings can show potential before a sale.

Staged photos tend to attract more interest, and virtual staging costs far less than renting furniture. Many markets and listing services require disclosure that images are digitally staged, and the room must not be misrepresented.

item.title: Yardi
item.description:
Yardi is one of the largest suppliers of software to the real estate industry. Property managers use it to market units, screen applicants, sign leases, collect rent, track maintenance, and run accounting. Different products fit different segments: Voyager serves larger portfolios, Breeze suits smaller operators, and other tools cover commercial space, senior living, and investment management.

AI features are collected under Virtuoso, which Yardi uses for tasks like answering resident questions, drafting leasing responses, handling invoices and documents, and analyzing performance. The goal is to take routine work off property staff and to provide insights from data that the company already holds in its accounting and leasing systems.

item.title: YNAB
item.description:
YNAB is as much a method as an app. Users assign each dollar of income to a category, such as rent, groceries, or savings, and update the plan as real spending happens. When money moves between categories, the app shows the tradeoff. The idea is to work from money you already have, not money you expect, which many people find reduces financial stress.

Features support that approach. Bank syncing imports transactions, goals track bills and savings targets, reports show spending trends, and shared budgets let partners manage money together. The company offers workshops and guides that teach the approach, which is a big part of why users stick with it. There is a mobile app and a web version.

item.title: pm-skills
item.description:
This repository bundles the following skills:

  • Opportunity Solution Tree: Structures desired outcomes into testable hypotheses.
  • Interview Script: Builds jobs-to-be-done customer research interview templates.
  • Product Strategy Canvas: A nine-section strategic planning template.
  • Value Proposition: A six-part jobs-to-be-done positioning framework.
  • Create PRD: Generates an eight-section product requirements document.
  • OKRs / Roadmaps: Aligns team objectives and roadmaps to company strategy.
  • Pre-Mortem: Identifies risks ahead of time using a Tiger/Elephant classification.
  • GTM Strategy: Plans channel, messaging, and launch activities.
  • Growth Loops: Designs self-sustaining growth flywheels.
  • North Star Metric: Selects a core metric and its supporting input metrics.
  • Cohort Analysis: Analyzes retention and engagement trends by cohort.

item.title: Product-Manager-Skills
item.description:
This repository bundles the following skills:

  • problem-framing-canvas: MITRE’s Look Inward/Outward/Reframe sequence.
  • positioning-statement: Geoffrey Moore template for market differentiation.
  • stakeholder-mapping: Power x Interest and Impact x Power grid analysis.
  • discovery-interview-prep: Mom Test-style interview planning.
  • prioritization-advisor: Context-driven framework selection, including RICE, ICE, and Kano.
  • prd-development: Structured PRD from problem through metrics.
  • user-story: Mike Cohn format with Gherkin acceptance criteria.
  • tam-sam-som-calculator: Market sizing in three modes.
  • business-health-diagnostic: SaaS health analysis across growth and retention.
  • battle-card-builder: Sales enablement content from research findings.

item.title: UnleashX
item.description:
UnleashX provides voice and workflow automation. Teams configure AI agents that handle phone conversations and carry out actions across systems, such as calling leads, qualifying them, updating records, and sending follow-ups. Rules define what the worker may do.

The platform presents these as digital employees for roles like sales development and support. Outbound calling needs consent and compliance with telemarketing rules, and AI voice agents should disclose themselves.

UnleashX is paid, and independent information is limited, so run a pilot first. Alternatives include Bland AI, Retell AI, Vapi, Synthflow, and 11x. UnleashX suits small teams automating calls and follow-ups.

item.title: Conduyt
item.description:
Conduyt takes an approach to CRM pricing that departs from the per-seat model. A team pays a single price no matter how many people use the product, which suits small sales teams and agencies that would otherwise pay for every added user.

The basics are familiar: a contact database, deal pipelines, and activity tracking, with AI features that draft follow-up messages, summarize interactions, and reduce routine data entry. Positioned as AI-native, it aims to have the software do the admin work that salespeople dislike.

item.title: AppFolio
item.description:
AppFolio runs the daily operations of a property management business. Staff list vacancies on rental sites, screen applicants, sign leases, collect rent online, and track maintenance requests and vendors. Owners receive statements and reports, and residents use a portal and app to pay and submit requests.

AI features take over routine communication. An assistant answers common tenant questions by text at any hour, qualifies leads, schedules showings, and flags maintenance requests that need attention. Analytics help managers see trends in occupancy, delinquency, and costs, and accounting tools are designed for property trust accounting.

item.title: Blend
item.description:
Blend builds software for lenders. Instead of paper forms and email, borrowers apply on a digital platform that collects information, connects to bank accounts and payroll sources to verify income and assets, and tracks the status of the application. Loan officers and processors see the file in a shared workflow.

Automation cuts the manual work in underwriting preparation. The platform pulls data from verified sources, checks documents, and flags missing or inconsistent items so staff can fix problems early. It covers mortgages, home equity, and consumer lending products, and integrates with loan origination systems and credit providers.

item.title: Boundless
item.description:
Boundless helps people navigate US immigration paperwork. Users answer questions in a guided flow, and the software builds the forms needed for a case, such as a marriage-based green card or naturalization. Checks flag missing information and inconsistencies that often cause delays.

Human experts remain part of the process. Plans include review by immigration attorneys or specialists, and customers can get help with responding to requests from authorities. Tracking tools show deadlines and the status of the case, and educational material explains steps and timelines.

item.title: BoxBrownie
item.description:
BoxBrownie serves real estate marketing. Agents and photographers upload listing photos, and editors, supported by AI, enhance the images by fixing exposure, correcting color, replacing dull skies, and removing clutter or distractions. Turnaround is typically quick, which suits fast-moving listings.

Virtual staging is a major product. The service places digital furniture and decor into photos of empty rooms so buyers can imagine the space, which costs far less than physical staging. Other services include twilight conversions, lawn improvements, and floor plans.

item.title: Canary Technologies
item.description:
Canary builds software for hotels. Guests can check in online before arrival, sign registration forms, verify identity, and pay deposits, which shortens lines at the front desk. After arrival, messaging lets them ask for towels, late checkout, or recommendations through text instead of calling.

An AI layer answers common questions and handles requests, routing issues to staff when needed. Upsell tools offer room upgrades and add-ons at the right moment, which brings extra revenue. Other products cover contactless payments, digital tipping, and a guest-facing digital tablet in rooms.

item.title: Daloopa
item.description:
Daloopa serves the finance professionals who build models from public company reports. Instead of typing numbers from filings into Excel, an analyst gets a database of financial line items pulled from documents like quarterly reports and presentations, with each number linked back to its source in the original file.

Updates arrive soon after companies report, so models stay current. An Excel add-in lets analysts pull data into their own templates, and an API and integrations with AI assistants allow data to flow into other workflows. The company has focused on accuracy and traceability, since errors in financial data are costly.

item.title: Deel
item.description:
Deel is a global hiring and payments platform. A company that wants to employ someone in another country can use Deel as the employer of record, which means Deel holds the legal employment relationship locally and handles contracts, payroll, benefits, and taxes. It also manages contractors, with agreements and payments in many currencies.

Beyond employment, Deel has built an HR suite covering global payroll for companies with their own entities, benefits, equipment, time tracking, and immigration support. AI features review and generate contracts against local rules, answer compliance questions, and automate workflows, which reduces the research that cross-border hiring requires.

item.title: Docketwise
item.description:
Docketwise is built specifically for immigration law. Attorneys collect information from clients with online questionnaires, and the software places answers on the correct government forms, which saves repeated typing. Because forms change, the platform keeps them updated.

It manages the rest of a case. Deadlines and receipts are tracked, status updates can be pulled from government sources, and client portals let people upload documents and see progress. Billing and email integrations support daily practice, and AI features help with drafting and summarizing.

item.title: Duve
item.description:
Duve is a guest experience platform. Before arrival, guests receive a digital check-in flow, can upload documents, and see offers for upgrades and extras. During the stay, a messaging assistant answers questions about the property and the area, and requests are routed to staff when a person is needed.

The platform includes a digital guidebook, upsell tools that present add-ons at the right moment, and integration with property management systems. For hoteliers and vacation rental managers, this reduces repetitive messages and brings extra revenue per booking.

item.title: Everlaw
item.description:
Everlaw helps legal teams work through evidence. Documents are uploaded, processed, and made searchable, and reviewers tag them, share notes, and build case narratives. Visual tools show relationships and timelines, and cloud delivery means teams can collaborate without installing software.

AI speeds up the work. Predictive coding ranks documents by likely relevance, clustering groups similar content, and generative features summarize documents, answer questions across a set, and draft deposition outlines. Everlaw has tools used by public interest lawyers and human rights investigators, and the company supports access programs.

item.title: Floify
item.description:
Floify handles the document stage of mortgage lending. Loan officers invite borrowers to a secure portal where they upload pay stubs, bank statements, and other items, sign disclosures electronically, and watch the status of their loan. The portal carries the lender’s branding.

Automation reduces manual follow-up. The system sends reminders for missing documents, sorts and labels uploads, and updates borrowers and real estate agents as milestones are reached. It connects to loan origination systems so data moves between them. Analytics show where loans get stuck.

item.title: FourKites
item.description:
FourKites is a supply chain visibility platform. It collects location and status data from carriers, telematics devices, and ocean and air sources, and shows shippers where each load is. Predictive estimates of arrival time account for traffic, weather, and dwell time at facilities, which are more accurate than static schedules.

Alerts warn teams of delays so they can reroute or notify customers. Yard and dock scheduling tools coordinate appointments, and analytics help identify problem carriers or lanes. AI agents handle tasks like checking on late shipments and communicating with carriers.

item.title: Gusto
item.description:
Gusto is built for employers without a dedicated HR department. A business adds its team, and Gusto calculates pay, withholds and files payroll taxes, and pays employees and contractors. Employees get pay stubs and benefits information in an app, and onboarding checklists collect forms and agreements from new hires.

The platform extends beyond payroll. It offers health insurance and retirement plan administration through partners, time tracking, hiring tools, and compliance support such as reminders and labor law guidance. AI features help flag likely filing errors, draft job descriptions and policies, and answer HR questions in plain language.

item.title: HiredScore
item.description:
HiredScore applies AI to the early stages of hiring. When applications arrive, it grades candidates against the requirements of the role, surfaces people who might be good fits, including past applicants and current employees, and helps recruiters focus on promising profiles first.

It integrates with applicant tracking systems and HR platforms, and Workday acquired the company to build AI into its talent products. Features include internal mobility recommendations, which help companies fill roles from within, and reporting to monitor process fairness and compliance.

item.title: Jobber
item.description:
Jobber is built for small service companies such as lawn care, cleaning, plumbing, and locksmith businesses. Owners send quotes, schedule jobs on a calendar, dispatch crews, and invoice customers, with a mobile app for the crew to see their route, take notes, and collect payment on site.

Client-facing features help win and keep work. Customers can request services online, approve quotes, pay invoices, and receive reminders and arrival notices, and a client hub keeps their history together. Automations send follow-ups and review requests. An AI assistant drafts messages and helps convert rough notes into a clear quote.

item.title: Kajabi
item.description:
Kajabi is an all-in-one platform for knowledge businesses. A creator builds a site, sells courses, memberships, coaching, and digital downloads, collects payments, runs email campaigns, and hosts a community, all from one dashboard instead of stitching together several tools.

Marketing and automation are built in. Landing pages, funnels, email sequences, and a pipeline for leads let creators sell without extra software. The AI assistant helps write copy, plan courses, and generate emails, and analytics show revenue and engagement. Mobile apps for members are available.

item.title: Moveworks
item.description:
Moveworks brings an assistant to employee support. Workers ask for help in Slack, Teams, or a portal, and the system understands the request, finds the answer in company knowledge, or completes the action by connecting to IT and HR systems. Common examples are unlocking an account, requesting software, or finding a policy.

The company grew by focusing on large enterprises and on language understanding specific to workplace requests. It added generative AI and agent capabilities, with a platform for building custom agents and connecting to many business systems.

item.title: Muck Rack
item.description:
Muck Rack is a public relations platform. PR professionals search its database to find journalists who cover a topic, see what they have written recently, and build media lists. They send pitches and track responses, and the platform monitors news to show where their company or clients are mentioned.

Reporting tools measure coverage by reach and sentiment, and dashboards show how campaigns perform. AI features summarize articles, suggest journalists, and help draft pitches, saving time on research and writing. The company also publishes research about the relationship between journalists and PR.

item.title: NationBuilder
item.description:
NationBuilder is designed for people building a movement. A campaign or organization keeps records of supporters, volunteers, and donors in one database, runs a website, sends email and texts, organizes events, and takes donations. Having everything together helps small teams manage a large network.

Tools support organizing, such as lists, tags, and tasks for volunteers, and reporting on progress toward goals. AI features help draft messages and summarize supporter information. The platform is used by campaigns, community groups, and associations around the world.

item.title: nCino
item.description:
nCino is cloud banking software. A bank uses it to manage the full lending process, from application to documents, analysis, approval, and closing, replacing paper and email chains. It covers commercial, consumer, and mortgage lending and account opening.

AI and automation reduce manual work. Models extract financial data from documents, assess credit risk, and flag items for review, and agents help with tasks like drafting credit memos. Dashboards give management visibility across the portfolio.

item.title: Noterro
item.description:
Noterro is built for small bodywork and rehab practices. Clients book online and fill in intake forms before arriving, and therapists record sessions with notes. An AI feature turns a few prompts into a structured SOAP note, saving time at the end of each appointment.

Other tools cover everyday needs: scheduling, reminders, payments, packages and memberships, and insurance claims where relevant. Reports track revenue and client retention.

Noterro is paid, with plans per practitioner. It is aimed at solo practitioners and small clinics. Alternatives include Jane, Cliniko, MassageBook, Vagaro, and SimplePractice. Noterro suits manual therapists who want simpler admin.

item.title: project44
item.description:
project44 is a supply chain visibility platform. It gathers location and status data from trucks, rail, ocean, and air carriers, merges it into one view, and shows shippers where each shipment is. Predictive ETAs account for traffic, weather, and port conditions.

Alerts flag delays early, so teams can reroute or notify customers. The platform also offers tools for appointment scheduling, drayage, and analytics on carrier performance, and AI features automate routine tracking tasks and communication.

item.title: Rogo
item.description:
Rogo focuses on the work of junior bankers and analysts, who spend hours digging through filings, transcripts, and data. A user asks a question in plain language, such as how a company’s margins compare with peers, and Rogo retrieves and analyzes the sources, citing where numbers came from.

It connects to financial data providers and a firm’s internal documents, produces outputs like comps and summaries, and fits into the workflow with tools such as Excel and PowerPoint. Security and compliance features suit regulated firms.

item.title: Sales Boomerang
item.description:
Sales Boomerang helps brokers stay in touch at the right time. It connects to a broker’s client list, watches for signals such as changes in credit, equity, or market rates, and alerts the broker when a former client might benefit from refinancing or a new purchase.

That turns a dormant database into leads. Automated outreach can follow, with messages personalized to the situation. Brokers use it to generate repeat and referral business without constant manual review.

item.title: SimplePractice
item.description:
SimplePractice is widely used by solo and small group private practices. Clients book appointments online, complete intake forms in a portal, and join video sessions, while clinicians keep notes, treatment plans, and billing in the same system. Insurance claims can be submitted electronically.

AI features help clinicians write progress notes from session details and speed up documentation, which is a chief burden for therapists. The platform offers reminders, reporting, and a client app for messaging and payments.

item.title: StyleSeat
item.description:
StyleSeat serves independent beauty professionals. Clients search for stylists, browse portfolios and reviews, and book appointments, while professionals manage their calendar, take deposits, and process payments through the platform.

The marketplace helps new clients find providers, and the business tools handle reminders, no-show protection, and client records. Recommendations use location and preference data to match clients.

StyleSeat has a subscription for professionals and fees on some transactions. Fees for marketplace clients can be a concern for stylists with an existing following. Alternatives include Vagaro, Fresha, Booksy, Square Appointments, and Glossgenius. StyleSeat suits independent stylists and barbers.

item.title: Vagaro
item.description:
Vagaro runs the front desk for beauty and wellness businesses. Clients book online or through a marketplace app, staff manage calendars, take payments, and track inventory. Reminders and no-show protection reduce lost appointments.

Marketing tools include email and text campaigns, loyalty programs, and a presence on the Vagaro marketplace. AI answers calls and messages, helps book appointments, and suggests promotions.

Vagaro charges a monthly fee per business, with add-ons and payment processing fees. Alternatives include Fresha, Booksy, StyleSeat, Square Appointments, and Mindbody. Vagaro suits salons, spas, and studios.

item.title: Visier
item.description:
Visier gathers data from HR systems into a model built for workforce questions. HR teams and managers explore metrics such as turnover, hiring speed, diversity, and compensation, and see how they vary by team and over time. Prebuilt analyses save the effort of building reports from scratch.

AI predicts who may leave, models the effect of decisions, and answers questions in plain language through a virtual assistant. Planning tools support headcount and cost scenarios, and integrations pull data from systems such as Workday and SAP.

item.title: Zycus
item.description:
Zycus is a source-to-pay suite. Companies manage supplier onboarding, sourcing events, contracts, purchase orders, and invoice processing in one platform, giving procurement teams visibility and control over spend.

AI agents assist with the work. They read contracts to extract terms, detect anomalies in pricing or invoices, suggest suppliers, and draft communications. Analytics show savings and compliance.

Zycus is sold to large enterprises on subscription. Alternatives include Coupa, SAP Ariba, Jaggaer, Ivalua, and GEP. Zycus suits procurement teams at large organizations.

item.title: Lettu
item.description:
Lettu is a platform for brands, agencies, and creators who work together. Influencer and creator campaigns involve briefs, contracts, approvals, payments, and usage rights, which are often handled in scattered emails. Lettu puts these into one workflow with legal templates drafted by lawyers.

The platform helps brands and agencies draft briefs, agree terms, track deliverables, and manage rights, such as how long content can be used. It draws on the law firm’s experience in advertising and media law, and AI features speed up drafting and review.

item.title: Astra for Law
item.description:
Astra for Law packages OpenAI’s model for legal work. Rather than a separate model, it pairs a general model with a dedicated search index of U.S. case law, statutes, regulations, and court rules, and instructions shaped for legal analysis and drafting. The goal is research answers that are grounded in sources a lawyer can check.

Access has been limited. OpenAI offered it first to selected firms through a trusted access program, with plans to make it available to legal technology companies through the API so they can build it into their own products. Partner plugins connect it to tools used in legal practice, such as document review, practice management, and document management systems.

item.title: QueryStory
item.description:
QueryStory approaches analytics with agents. A team connects its data sources and describes the business, such as its metrics and definitions, and then asks questions in natural language. The agents write queries, analyze results, and respond with explanations and visuals.

The point is to go beyond a static chart. When a number moves, a user can ask why, and the agent investigates by looking at breakdowns and related data. Business context helps the agent interpret questions the way an analyst on the team would.

item.title: Encore AI
item.description:
Encore AI builds on conversation data. It analyzes recordings of calls and chats to learn which behaviors lead to good outcomes, such as how top reps handle objections or open a conversation. Those patterns become the basis for AI agents that talk with customers.

The agents can take calls or messages themselves or support human reps with live guidance. The idea is to scale the best performers’ approach across a team instead of relying on training alone. Companies with large volumes of calls and recorded history are the target.

item.title: Dataiku
item.description:
Dataiku aims to let analysts, data scientists, and engineers work in the same environment. Teams connect to data sources, clean and prepare data with visual recipes or code, build models, and deploy them as applications or services. The visual interface lowers the barrier for business users, while coders can use notebooks and libraries.

The platform has added tools for generative AI, including connecting to language models, building retrieval applications, and creating agents. Governance features track models and projects, assess risk, and document decisions, which large organizations need to meet internal and regulatory requirements.

item.title: Born to Found
item.description:
Born to Found guides first-time founders through the early journey. It divides company building into stages, such as validating an idea, building a first product, and finding customers, and supplies playbooks and checklists for each, so a founder knows what to focus on at their point.

An AI coach answers questions and reviews work, drawing on the founder’s stage and project details. This offers a low-cost alternative to mentors for people who lack access to experienced advisors, and a structure to keep going when the path is unclear.

item.title: SwiftAlerts
item.description:
SwiftAlerts gathers market data into a structure that agents can query. Instead of hunting through separate sources, an agent can ask about relationships between trades, holdings, filings, and sentiment, and get connected answers.

The idea fits the rise of AI agents that research and monitor markets. Reliable data is essential, since trading decisions on wrong information lose money, and nothing from such a tool is financial advice.

Independent information is limited, so check data sources, update speed, and terms. SwiftAlerts is free to start. Alternatives include Unusual Whales, Quiver Quantitative, Benzinga, Polygon.io, and Financial Datasets. SwiftAlerts suits developers building market agents, with caution.

item.title: Anomaly AI
item.description:
Anomaly AI is for people who work with data that is too big or messy for a normal spreadsheet. A user uploads Excel or CSV files or connects sources such as databases, warehouses, and Google Sheets, then asks questions in natural language. The tool answers with tables, charts, and written explanations.

The vendor emphasizes traceable answers, meaning the analysis is run as code against the data so results can be inspected and not just generated by a language model. It can merge files with database data in one analysis, find trends, and flag unusual values. A connector allows assistants like Claude to hand questions about your data to the service.

item.title: Igly
item.description:
Igly focuses on product images. A seller uploads photos of items, and the tool removes or replaces backgrounds, places products in lifestyle scenes, adjusts lighting, and creates variations for marketplaces. An infinite canvas lets users arrange and edit many images in one project.

Agents handle multi-step edits from a plain description, such as producing a set of listing images in a consistent style. Presets match the dimensions and rules of common platforms. Sellers use it to reduce the cost of photography and design.

item.title: Amplemarket
item.description:
Amplemarket helps sales teams find and contact potential customers. It combines a database of B2B contacts and companies with search filters and intent signals, so reps can build lists of people who match their ideal customer and show signs of interest, such as hiring, funding, or website activity. Contact data is verified and enriched to reduce bounced emails and wrong numbers.

Outreach happens through multichannel sequences that mix email, phone calls, and social steps such as LinkedIn messages. A parallel dialer lets reps call through lists quickly. The AI layer researches each account and prospect, drafts personalized emails and call notes, and surfaces the best people to contact first. Duo Intelligence is Amplemarket’s approach of AI preparing the work while the rep reviews and sends, instead of fully automatic sending.

item.title: Arcade
item.description:
Arcade makes interactive demos simple to create. A person records their screen using a Chrome extension, and Arcade turns the clicks into a step-by-step walkthrough with highlights and captions. The result can be edited, branded, and shared as a link or embedded on a website or in an email.

Teams use demos for several purposes. Marketing places them on landing pages to show a product in action, sales sends them to prospects, and customer success uses them for onboarding and help content. AI features add voiceovers, generate captions, and personalize demos by changing names and details. Analytics show who watched and where they stopped.

item.title: C3.ai
item.description:
C3.ai builds packaged AI applications and a platform for developing them. Instead of starting from scratch, a company can adopt an application for a defined problem, such as predicting when equipment will fail, detecting fraud, or optimizing inventory, and connect it to their data. The platform provides tools for data integration, modeling, and deployment.

The company has moved to add generative AI. Its offerings include tools that let users ask questions about enterprise data in natural language and agent features for business workflows. Customers include utilities, manufacturers, banks, and defense and government agencies, where large-scale deployments are common.

item.title: ChurnZero
item.description:
ChurnZero is built for customer success teams at software-as-a-service companies.
